name: Rutherford’s concentrated-charge atomic model
description: Concentrated atomic charge as an explanation of large-angle scattering.

impact.note: Known to scientists rather than the public, it gave the atom a nucleus; atomic theory, nuclear physics and their many applications all rest on it.

date.label: May 1911
date.basis: Month of the published paper, not the earlier scattering observations.

events.statement: In the May 1911 paper Rutherford used Geiger–Marsden observations and an intense concentrated atomic charge to account for large-angle scattering.

evidence.supports: In the May 1911 paper Rutherford used Geiger–Marsden observations and an intense concentrated atomic charge to account for large-angle scattering.

earliest_record.rationale: A dated witness in the inspected evidence, not a global-priority claim.

caveats: The credited observations date from 1909 and 1910. A February 1911 oral account is mentioned. The model predates the neutron and modern nuclear theory.
